info.title: Embedded Accounting API
info.description: The Embedded Accounting API enables you to create and manage ledger information, taxes, transactions, bank data, subscriptions, and financial reports.

x-tagGroups.name: Compliance
x-tagGroups.description: Manage compliance obligations, meet deadlines and avoid penalties.

x-tagGroups.name: Dimensions
x-tagGroups.description: Analyze data using dimensions to filter transactions.

x-tagGroups.name: Entities
x-tagGroups.description: Manage and look up entity data such as customers, suppliers, sub-types, and address locales.

x-tagGroups.name: Ledger
x-tagGroups.description: Configure and work with accounting periods and nominal ledger accounts.

x-tagGroups.name: Organisation
x-tagGroups.description: Create account invitations and manage business relationships.

x-tagGroups.name: Subscriptions
x-tagGroups.description: Manage your customer's subscriptions to Sage Embedded Accounting.

x-tagGroups.name: Tax
x-tagGroups.description: Manage and apply taxes in supported legislative regions.

tags.name: Authorization
tags.description: An operation provided by the Sage Identity service for authenticating and authorizing client applications. Note that this operation is served from a different URL to the rest of the Embedded Accounting API.

tags.name: Banking Cloud
tags.description: Operations for handling connections between [bank accounts](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/bank/bankaccounts) in the real world and in the Sage platform.

tags.name: Payments Acceptance
tags.description: Operations relating to the Bank Service's integration with third-party payments providers.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Operations relating to a tenant's products and their sales and purchase configurations.

tags.name: Ledger account properties
tags.description: Operations relating to ledger account properties.

tags.name: Taxes
tags.description: Retrieve the deductible tax percentage, if one exists.

tags.name: Tax Treatments
tags.description: Define how taxes are treated for the purposes of reporting. See also [Tax treatments](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/tax/taxtreatments).

tags.name: Tax Codes
tags.description: Define and manage tax codes that classify transactions for tax calculation and reporting. See also [Tax codes](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/tax/taxcodes).

tags.name: Tax Item Types
tags.description: Differentiate types of sales or purchases for compliance purposes and, in conjunction with tax treatments, determine how a transaction should be handled.

tags.name: Tax Rates
tags.description: A combination of tax treatment, tax item type, and tax code which determines the tax percentage to apply to a transaction. See also [Tax rates](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/tax/taxrates).

tags.name: Tax Groups
tags.description: Used to collate useful combinations of treatments, types, codes, and regions that can be applied in a simple way through UI.

tags.name: Tax Schemes
tags.description: Different tax schemes can be selected to apply to different accounting periods. See also [Tax schemes](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/tax/taxschemes).

tags.name: Withholding Types
tags.description: Configure deduction rates to apply to transactions under certain schemes in particular legislations, such as the Construction Industry Scheme in the UK.

tags.name: Allocations
tags.description: Operations relating to [allocation](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/payments/paymentsallocations) links between existing payment transactions and trade documents.

tags.name: Journals
tags.description: Operations for handling [journals](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/journals/journals) in a generic configurable way.

tags.name: Payments
tags.description: Operations for creating and managing [payment](/embedded-accounting/docs/latest/guides/accounting-data-schema/payments/payments) transactions, such as customer receipts and customer refunds, and their allocations against trade documents.

tags.name: Sales invoice settings
tags.description: Operations for handling sales invoice settings.

get.summary: v1 - Generate URL to download attachment
get.description:
Generates a short-lived URL to download an attachment representing a file in a tenant.

This operation returns a download URL only if the attachment status is `Complete`. When the attachment status is `Pending`, repeatedly calling this operation may result in `HTTP 429 Too many requests`. To avoid this, do one of the following:

* Check the attachment status before calling this operation.
* Call this operation using an exponential backoff retry pattern.

schema.title: V1GetAttachmentsResponseModel
schema.description: Response model for the V1GetAttachments operation.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the attachment.

ParentId.description: The unique identifier of the folder where the attachment is stored. Returns `null` if the attachment is not stored against a folder.

Status.description:
The attachment status. 

Valid values:

* `Pending` Uploading the attachment to an Amazon S3 bucket.
* `Verifying` Scanning the attachment for viruses and checking if the attachment type is supported by the service.
* `Complete` The service has successfully uploaded the attachment to an Amazon S3 bucket. The attachment type has been verified as supported and virus scan found no viruses in the attachment.
* `Quarantined` The service has successfully uploaded the attachment to an Amazon S3 bucket, but the attachment was quarantined because virus scan found a virus.
* `FileTooLarge` The attachment exceeds the file size limit.
* `InvalidFileType` The MIME type specified in the attachment metadata is not supported or does not match the actual MIME type of the file.

Filename.description: The name of the attachment (a file, a folder, or a URL link) displayed in the user interface.

Filesize.description: The size of the attachment file in kilobytes.

Description.description: The attachment description.

MimeType.description: The MIME type of the attachment. For supported MIME types, see [Supported attachments](/sxp/apis/attachments-service/latest/attachments/supported-attachments).

ApplicationFileType.description: The application file type to which the attachment belongs.

IsHidden.description: Indicates whether the attachment is hidden.

Keywords.description: The key-value pairs assigned to the attachment.

Key.description: The name of the key assigned to the attachment.

Value.description: The value defined for the key.

Ttl.description: Specifies the number of hours the attachment will be stored. After this period, the attachment is automatically and permanently deleted. If this parameter is blank, the attachment is stored indefinitely.

CreatedAt.description: The UTC Epoch timestamp (including milliseconds) when the attachment was created.

CreatedBy.description: The unique identifier of the principal that called the API to create the attachment.

CreatedByUser.description: The details of the user that created the attachment.

UserId.description: The unique identifier of the user.

FirstName.description: The first name of the user.

LastName.description: The last name of the user.

UpdatedAt.description: The UTC Epoch timestamp (including milliseconds) when the attachment was last updated.

UpdatedBy.description: The unique identifier of the principal that called the API to update the attachment.

UpdatedByUser.description: The details of the user that last updated the attachment.

UserId.description: The unique identifier of the user.

FirstName.description: The first name of the user.

LastName.description: The last name of the user.

schema.title: V1GetBankAccountsResponseModel
schema.description: Response Model for V1 Get Bank Accounts request.

Id.description: The UUID of the bank account.

Name.description: The name of the bank account.

BankName.description: The business name of the associated financial institution.

External.description: The external details of the bank account.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the bank account in the external source system that generated it.

Source.description: The external source that generated the bank account.

IsActive.description: Specifies whether the account is visible in the bank account list. An inactive account is hidden from the user interface but is not deleted from the system, and postings can still be made to it.

AccountNumber.description: The bank account number.

CreditCardNumber.description: The last four digits of a credit card number associated with this bank account.

CurrencyIso.description: The three-letter currency code of the bank account, in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format.

BIC_SWIFT.description: The bank account BIC or SWIFT code.

Debit.description: The sum of debit values for the bank account.

Base.description: The sum of all item debits in the tenant's base currency.

Currency.description: The sum of all item debits in the currency of the bank account, as defined by `CurrencyIso`.

Credit.description: The sum of credit values for the bank account.

Base.description: The sum of all item credits in the tenant's base currency.

Currency.description: The sum of all item credits in the currency of the bank account, as defined by `CurrencyIso`.

Base.description: The balance in the tenant's base currency.

Currency.description: The balance in the currency of the bank account, as defined by `CurrencyIso`.

BankFeedBalance.description: The account balance in the bank feed.

Base.description: The balance in the tenant's base currency in the bank feed.

Currency.description: The balance in the currency of the bank account, as defined by `CurrencyIso` in the bank feed.

BankFeedId.description: The bank account's bank feed ID.

PaymentsAcceptance.description: Payments acceptance details for this bank account.

PayeeBankAccountId.description: The unique ID of the bank account that is used to receive payments from this bank account.

ProviderId.description: The ID of the payments provider linked to this bank account, for example, Stripe.

AccountId.description: The unique ID of the PAS account associated with this bank account.

BankFeedLastBalanceDate.description: The UTC date and time, in [RFC 3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.html#section-5.6) format, when the bank balance was updated by the bank feed.

BankFeedLastTransactionDate.description: The UTC date and time, in [RFC 3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.html#section-5.6) format, when the last transaction was imported by the bank feed.

LedgerAccountId.description: The UUID of the associated ledger account.

ImportTransactionWorkflowStatusId.description: The unique ID of the status of the Import Transactions workflow.

ImportTransactionWorkflowStatus.description: The status of the current Import Transactions workflow for this bank account.

Status.description: Status of the workflow.

BankFeedPlaceholderBankUsed.description: Specifies whether Banking Cloud is using a placeholder bank (used for file imports), or a real-world bank.

BankFeedStatus.description: The status of the account record held by Banking Cloud and referenced by the `BankFeedId` property. Possible values are: `active`, `authRequired`, `cancelled`, `connecting`, `inactiveClient`, `inactiveFeed`, `invalid`, `notConnected`, `pending`, `verifyingAuth`. Note: This value is cached and is only updated when a new account is created in Banking Cloud, or when a call is made to the [Get bank account connection status](#tag/Bank-Accounts/operation/V1GetConnectionStatusById) endpoint.

BankFeedStatusLastUpdatedAt.description: The UTC date and time, in [RFC 3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.html#section-5.6) format, when the cached `BankFeedStatus` property was last updated.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the tenant.

put.summary: V1 - Retrieve income and expenditure obligations from HMRC
put.description: Retrieves income and expenditure obligations for the report year from HMRC. When `X-Accountant-On-Behalf` contains an accountant business ID, the request must be made by a Sage Platform M2M principal and the supplied business must have an active client relationship where `BusinessId` is the supplied accountant business and `RelatedBusinessId` is the client business. The accountant business is used to resolve the Sage Network dataset and connection; all client tax and compliance data remains scoped to the client business. When the header is omitted, the existing client-business connection resolution is used.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

LastRunDate.description: The most recent date the report was generated or processed.

Turnover.description: Total business income before deducting expenses.

Other.description: Income from outside the business's main trading activity that still counts as part of total turnover for tax purposes.

TaxTakenOffTradingIncome.description: Income Tax already deducted from trading income at source, before the business received it. For example, for the Construction Industry Scheme.

CostOfGoodsAllowable.description: The cost of goods bought and used in the process of selling goods or services, which can be deducted from income for tax purposes.

PaymentsToSubcontractorsAllowable.description: The amount paid to subcontractors, considered an allowable business expense by HMRC. Can be deducted from income when calculating taxable profit.

WagesAndStaffCostsAllowable.description: Wages, salaries, and staff-related costs that HMRC allows to be deducted as business expenses when calculating taxable profit.

CarVanTravelExpensesAllowable.description: Travel-related business expenses for using cars, vans, or other vehicles, that can be deducted for tax purposes.

PremisesRunningCostsAllowable.description: Day-to-day running costs of business premises, including home office space, that HMRC allows to be deducted as expenses when calculating taxable profit.

MaintenanceCostsAllowable.description: Business costs of maintaining, servicing, or repairing equipment, tools, or premises that HMRC allows to be deducted as expenses when calculating taxable profit. Running and operational costs, not improvements or upgrades.

AdminCostsAllowable.description: Business-related administrative costs that HMRC allows to be deducted from income when calculating taxable profit. Expenses necessary for day-to-day operations, but not directly tied to the production of goods or services.

InterestOnBankOtherLoansAllowable.description: Interest paid on business loans, credit facilities, or bank overdrafts that HMRC allows to be deducted as an allowable business expense when calculating taxable profit. Includes the interest portion of any loans or credit used for business purposes.

FinanceChargesAllowable.description: Charges related to obtaining or servicing business finance that HMRC allows to be deducted as allowable business expenses. Includes business-related fees and interest associated with loans, credit facilities, or finance agreements.

IrrecoverableDebtsAllowable.description: Bad debts written off as uncollectible, which HMRC allows to be deducted as an allowable business expense when calculating taxable profit. Debts that were previously recorded as income but now deemed unlikely to be recovered.

ProfessionalFeesAllowable.description: Fees paid for professional services necessary for running the business, which HMRC allows to be deducted as business expenses when calculating taxable profit.

DepreciationAllowable.description: The reduction in value of business assets such as equipment, machinery, or vehicles that HMRC allows to be accounted for as an expense. HMRC does not directly allow depreciation as an expense, but Capital Allowances claims can be made to account for the depreciation of assets.

OtherExpensesAllowable.description: Business expenses necessary for running the business that don't fall into specific categories like wages, rent, or vehicle costs, but still deductible from business income to reduce taxable profit.

AdvertisingCostsAllowable.description: Expenses incurred for promoting the business, that HMRC allows to be deducted when calculating taxable profit. Costs directly related to marketing the business to generate income.

BusinessEntertainmentCostsAllowable.description: Costs of entertaining clients, customers, or potential clients, that HMRC allows to be claimed as business expenses when calculating taxable profit. Associated with social events or hospitality designed to promote the business or secure future business.

Additions.description: Assets or costs added to the value of an asset pool or balance during the tax year. This could include purchases of new, or upgrades to existing assets.

CostOfGoodsDisallowable.description: Costs related to goods used, bought, or produced for the business, but which HMRC does not allow deduction of when calculating taxable profit.

PaymentsToSubcontractorsDisallowable.description: Payments made to subcontractors that cannot be claimed as allowable business expenses when calculating taxable profit.

WagesAndStaffCostsDisallowable.description: Wages, salaries, bonuses, or staff-related costs that HMRC does not allow to be deducted when calculating taxable profit, usually because the expense isn’t fully for business purposes or fails to meet compliance rules.

CarVanTravelExpensesDisallowable.description: Travel or vehicle-related costs that HMRC does not allow to be claimed as tax-deductible, usually because the expense includes personal use, or doesn't qualify as wholly and exclusively for business.

PremisesRunningCostsDisallowable.description: Costs for running the business property, such as rent or utilities, that HMRC does not allow to be deducted when calculating taxable profit, usually because they include private use, or aren't exclusively for business purposes.

MaintenanceCostsDisallowable.description: Repairs and maintenance expenses that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, typically because they are for personal use, capital in nature, or not genuinely business-related.

AdminCostsDisallowable.description: Administrative or office-related costs that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, usually because they relate to personal use, or lack business justification.

InterestOnBankOtherLoansDisallowable.description: Interest payments on loans or overdrafts that HMRC does not allow as a business expense, typically because they relate to non-business borrowing, or fall outside what’s considered wholly and exclusively for business purposes.

FinanceChargesDisallowable.description: Finance-related costs that HMRC does not allow to be deducted when calculating taxable profit, because they’re not wholly for business purposes or outside HMRC’s definition of allowable finance charges.

IrrecoverableDebtsDisallowable.description: Bad debts that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, usually because they don’t meet the criteria for being a genuine business loss, or a proper attempt has not been made to recover them.

ProfessionalFeesDisallowable.description: Fees paid for professional services that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, typically because they aren’t related to business activities or are considered personal or non-essential.

DepreciationDisallowable.description: The portion of depreciation that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, typically because it’s not an allowable form of expense for tax purposes under HMRC rules.

OtherExpensesDisallowable.description: Other business expenses that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, usually because they are not wholly and exclusively for business use or don’t meet the criteria for allowable expenses.

AdvertisingCostsDisallowable.description: Advertising or promotional expenses that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, usually because they are considered personal or not directly related to business operations.

BusinessEntertainmentCostsDisallowable.description: Entertainment expenses that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit, typically because they are considered personal, excessive, or not directly related to business activities.

TotalExpenses.description: The total amount of expenses the business has incurred during the specific period, which can include both allowable and disallowable expenses.

Allowable.description: The total amount of business expenses that HMRC allows to be deducted from taxable profit, as long as they are incurred wholly and exclusively for the purpose of running the business.

Disallowable.description: The total amount of business expenses that HMRC does not allow to be deducted from taxable profit.

NetProfit.description: The amount the business has earned after all allowable and disallowable expenses have been subtracted from total revenue.

NetLoss.description: The amount by which the business's total expenses exceed its total revenue for the specified period.

schema.description: The response containing UK property period summary data.

FromDate.description: The start date of the period summary, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

ToDate.description: The end date of the period summary, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

Income.description: Income details for the UK property period.

PremiumsOfLeaseGrant.description: Premium paid by an existing tenant to induce a new tenant to enter into a leasehold agreement.

ReversePremiums.description: The total amount of reverse premiums, including ground rents, rent charges and Rent a Room rental income.

PeriodAmount.description: Total rental and property related income.

TaxDeducted.description: Tax deducted from property related income.

RentsReceived.description: Total rent received under the Rent a Room scheme.

Expenses.description: Expenses details for the UK property period.

PremisesRunningCosts.description: Fixed costs relating to the property, such as rent, rates and insurance.

FinancialCosts.description: Loan interest and other financial costs.

ProfessionalFees.description: Legal, management and other professional fees.

CostOfServices.description: Cost of services provided, including wages.

ResidentialFinancialCost.description: The residential financial cost that is deductible from rental income (tax relief).

TravelCosts.description: Travel costs incurred as part of property letting activities.

ResidentialFinancialCostsCarriedForward.description: Amount of relief for residential property finance costs carried forward.

AmountClaimed.description: Total amount of expenses claimed under the Rent a Room scheme.

ConsolidatedExpenses.description: The total consolidated expenses for the UK property period.

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds to wait before retrying.

TaxYear.description: The report year of the self-employment annual submission.

HMRCBusinessId.description: The unique identifier of the business at HMRC.

Action.description: The action to be performed on the submission.

StatementType.description: The type of personal tax self-employment statement. `TradingAllowance` relates to day-to-day business income and expenses. `CapitalAllowance` relates to assets.

Data.description: Submission payload containing adjustments and allowances for the tax year.

Adjustments.description: Adjustments applied to accounting profit for tax purposes.

IncludedNonTaxableProfits.description: Profits included in accounts that are not taxable and should be deducted.

BasisAdjustment.description: An adjustment arising from basis period changes, including spreading where applicable.

OverlapReliefUsed.description: Overlap relief set against profits in the year.

AccountingAdjustment.description: Accounting adjustments to reconcile profit to the tax calculation.

AveragingAdjustment.description: A tax relief adjustment applying mainly to farmers and creative artists.

OutstandingBusinessIncome.description: Outstanding business income brought into charge, such as late receipts.

BalancingChargeBpra.description: Balancing charge relating to Business Premises Renovation Allowance.

BalancingChargeOther.description: Other balancing charges brought into taxable profits.

GoodsAndServicesOwnUse.description: An adjustment for goods and services taken for personal use.

TransitionProfitAmount.description: The amount of transition profit arising from a move of tax year.

TransitionProfitAccelerationAmount.description: The portion of transition profit accelerated into the year.

Allowances.description: Capital and other allowances claimed for the period.

TradingIncomeAllowance.description: Trading allowance claimed, to a maximum £1,000.

CapitalAllowanceMainPool.description: The written-down allowance for the main capital pool.

CapitalAllowanceSpecialRatePool.description: The written-down allowance for the special rate pool.

EnhancedCapitalAllowance.description: Enhanced capital allowance claimed for qualifying energy and water efficient assets.

AllowanceOnSales.description: Capital allowance claimed on disposals or sales.

CapitalAllowanceSingleAssetPool.description: The allowance claimed for a single asset pool.

Amount.description: SBA amount claimed for this building.

FirstYear.description: First-year qualifying details for the building.

QualifyingDate.description: The date the building first qualified for SBA use.

QualifyingAmountExpenditure.description: Qualifying construction expenditure for SBA purposes.

Building.description: Details of the building the SBA relates to.

Name.description: The building name.

Number.description: The building number.

EnhancedStructuredBuildingAllowance.description: Enhanced Structures and Buildings Allowance, for example, for freeports or investment zones.

Amount.description: The enhanced SBA amount claimed for this building.

FirstYear.description: First-year qualifying details for the enhanced SBA.

QualifyingDate.description: The date the enhanced SBA first qualified.

Building.description: Details of the building the enhanced SBA relates to.

Name.description: The building name.

Number.description: The building number.

BusinessDetailsChangedRecently.description: Whether the business details have changed recently.

Class4NicsExemptionReason.description: The reason for exemption from Class 4 National Insurance contributions.

Status.description: Whether the submission has been completed.

WorkflowStatusId.description: The unique identifier of the workflow status.

ComplianceReportInstanceId.description: The unique identifier of the compliance report instance.

TaxYear.description: The tax year of the submission.

HMRCBusinessId.description: The identifier of the business at HMRC.

TradingName.description: The trading name of the business.

schema.title: requestmodel.v1
schema.description: Request model for managing UK Property Business Annual Submission.

TaxYear.description: The tax year for which the annual submission is being made.

HMRCBusinessId.description: The unique identifier of the HMRC business.

Action.description: The action to perform on the submission.

StatementType.description: The type of statement being submitted.

Data.description: UK property business annual submission data.

BalancingCharge.description: Corrects capital allowance value if too much tax relief has been applied to an asset.

PrivateUseAdjustment.description: Restricts tax relief on non-business assets.

BusinessPremisesRenovationAllowanceBalan.description: Arise when BPRA was claimed on a property which was later sold, or stopped being used, within a specified period. HMRC recovers some or all of the BPRA claimed with this charge.

NonResidentLandlord.description: Indicates whether the landlord is non-resident.

JointlyLet.description: Indicates whether the property is jointly let.

Allowances.description: Allowances for the UK property business.

AnnualInvestmentAllowance.description: Lets a business deduct the full cost of qualifying capital assets from taxable profits in the year of purchase, instead of spreading over several years.

BusinessPremisesRenovationAllowance.description: Business premises renovation allowance. Tax relief for renovating unused or derelict commercial buildings.

StructuredBuildingAllowance.description: Structured building allowance. Tax relief for the cost of constructing or renovating commercial buildings that would not otherwise qualify for capital allowances.

Amount.description: The allowance amount.

Name.description: Building name.

Number.description: Building number.

EnhancedStructuredBuildingAllowance.description: A higher-rate version of the standard structured building allowance.

Amount.description: The allowance amount.

Name.description: Building name.

Number.description: Building number.

ZeroEmissionsCarAllowance.description: Capital allowances relief available when a business buys a zero-emission car and wants to deduct the cost against taxable profits.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. parameters.description: The inclusive start date of the period to filter transactions, as a UTC date-time. Example: 2025-04-06T00:00:00.000Z. The maximum date range between FromDate and ToDate should not exceed 732 days.

parameters.name: ToDate
parameters.description: The inclusive end date of the period to filter transactions, as a UTC date-time. Example: 2026-04-05T00:00:00.000Z. The maximum date range between FromDate and ToDate should not exceed 732 days.

parameters.name: OnlyOpenItems
parameters.description: Limits the extraction to unpaid or not reversed charges. Example: false. When set to false, either the date range (FromDate and ToDate) or DocNumber should be supplied. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: RemovePOA
parameters.description: Remove Payment on Account details. Example: false. When true, details of any payments that the customer has made will not be returned. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: CustomerPaymentInformation
parameters.description: Include customer payment information. Example: false. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: IncludeEstimatedCharges
parameters.description: Include statistical (estimated) values for monthly payments. Example: true. Defaults to false.

delete.description: Deletes a state benefit in HMRC for the specified tax year.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. schema.description: Response Model for a V1 GetDimensionRules request.

items.description: Details of the dimension rule object.

Id.description: Unique ID of the dimension rule.

Code.description: A unique, human-readable value identifying the dimension rule.

OwnerType.description: An entity used in conjunction with `Dimension.Id` to define the objects available to a given rule. A tenant is supplied a template based on its region and business type. Each template contains a list of valid owner types, for example, Customer or Supplier, and a list of valid dimensions such as Department or Cost Centre. Within a rule, the dimension and owner types combine to determine which objects to allow. For example, in the UK, a rule with the dimension ID 'CustomerGroup' and the owner type 'Customer' prevents access to the `UpdateTagBalance` object. Template rules can be amended but not be deleted; rules created by the tenant can be deleted. See Type values in the left-hand menu for a complete list of valid types.

Id.description: Unique ID of the dimension.

Name.description: Name of the dimension.

IsMandatory.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule is mandatory.

SelectionType.description: Selection type of the dimension rule. This determines whether the dimension can be applied to single or multiple object types. For example, a dimension could be made available solely within sales records, or it could be available to both sales and product records.

DefaultTagId.description: Unique ID of the default tag associated to the dimension for this dimension rule.

UpdateTagBalance.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows the tag balance to be updated. When true, the value of entries specifying this dimension is included in the debits and credits apportioned to it.

AllowBalanceLimit.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule respects a balance limit set by the consuming application.

AllowColors.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows dimension tags to display colours through the consuming UI.

AllowAllocations.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows the use of allocations. The Transaction Service uses allocations to split costs between multiple business functions. This assists with financial reporting.

ValidateTags.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule requires tag validation. The Transaction Service validates whether a tag is allowed for certain transaction and dimension types.

ValidateLedgerAccount.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule requires ledger account validation. The Transaction Service validates whether a ledger account is allowed for certain transaction type and dimension types.

IsActive.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule is active. If false, dimensions and tags applied by the rule will not be available to select.

CreatedByTenant.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule was created by the tenant (true) or derives from the template (false).

X-Pagination-ItemsPerPage.description: Number of records returned per page.

schema.title: V1GetDimensionRuleByIdResponseModel
schema.description: Response Model for a V1 GetDimensionRuleById request

Id.description: Unique ID of the dimension rule.

Code.description: A unique, human-readable value identifying the dimension rule.

OwnerType.description: An entity used in conjunction with `Dimension.Id` to define the objects available to a given rule. A tenant is supplied a template based on its region and business type. Each template contains a list of valid owner types, for example, Customer or Supplier, and a list of valid dimensions such as Department or Cost Centre. Within a rule, the dimension and owner types combine to determine which objects to allow. For example, in the UK, a rule with the dimension ID 'CustomerGroup' and the owner type 'Customer' prevents access to the `UpdateTagBalance` object. Template rules can be amended but not be deleted; rules created by the tenant can be deleted. See Type values in the left-hand menu for a complete list of valid types.

Id.description: Unique ID of the dimension.

Name.description: Name of the dimension.

IsMandatory.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule is mandatory.

SelectionType.description: Selection type of the dimension rule. This determines whether the dimension can be applied to single or multiple object types. For example, a dimension could be made available solely within sales records, or it could be available to both sales and product records.

DefaultTagId.description: Unique ID of the default tag associated to the dimension for this dimension rule.

UpdateTagBalance.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows the tag balance to be updated. When true, the value of entries specifying this dimension is included in the debits and credits apportioned to it.

AllowBalanceLimit.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule respects a balance limit set by the consuming application.

AllowColors.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows dimension tags to display colours through the consuming UI.

AllowAllocations.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule allows the use of allocations. The Transaction Service uses allocations to split costs between multiple business functions. This assists with financial reporting.

ValidateTags.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule requires tag validation. The Transaction Service validates whether a tag is allowed for certain transaction and dimension types.

ValidateLedgerAccount.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule requires ledger account validation. The Transaction Service validates whether a ledger account is allowed for certain transaction type and dimension types.

IsActive.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule is active. If false, dimensions and tags applied by the rule will not be available to select.

CreatedAt.description: The [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time the dimension rule was created.

CreatedBy.description: Unique ID of the principal that created the dimension rule.

CreatedByTenant.description: Specifies whether the dimension rule was created by the tenant (true) or derives from the template (false).

DeletedBy.description: Unique ID of the principal that deleted the dimension tag.

DeletedAt.description: The [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time the dimension rule was deleted.

UpdatedBy.description: Unique ID of the principal that last updated the dimension rule.

UpdatedAt.description: The [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date-time the dimension rule was last updated.

post.description:
Creates a customer. A value must be provided for at least one of `AddressLine1`, `AddressLine2`, `Province`, `City`, `Suburb`, `PostCode` or `CountryCode`.

Requests are not de-duplicated. If the same request is submitted multiple times with different idempotency keys, multiple customers are created. If the idempotency key submitted has been used previously, the `Id` of the customer created in the original request is returned.

If an `External.Id` value is included, this is returned as the new record's `Id`. If the `External.Id` already exists for a customer, a new `Id` is automatically generated. It is therefore possible for multiple customer records to have the same `External.Id`, but only the first one created uses that as its primary record `Id`.

parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

Creates a supplier. A value must be provided for at least one of `AddressLine1`, `AddressLine2`, `Province`, `City`, `Suburb`, `PostCode` or `CountryCode`.

Requests are not de-duplicated. If the same request is submitted multiple times with different idempotency keys, multiple suppliers are created. If the idempotency key submitted has been used previously, the `Id` of the supplier created in the original request is returned.

If an `External.Id` value is included, this is returned as the new record's `Id`. If the `External.Id` already exists for a supplier, a new `Id` is automatically generated. It is therefore possible for multiple supplier records to have the same `External.Id`, but only the first one created uses that as its primary record `Id`.

put.description:
Updates the given supplier and child objects with one API call. Differs from the PATCH operation by allowing `Addresses`, `EmailAddresses` and `PhoneNumbers` to be updated. Also functions differently to the PATCH by passing its payload to the ERM Service in only one interaction.

Unless updating `Addresses`, `EmailAddresses` and `PhoneNumbers`, choose whether the PUT or the PATCH best fits your use case. For example, if your UI uses a single *Save* button beneath a record, the PUT operation is the best choice. If you save the record as the user tabs from field to field, the PATCH is preferable.

PeriodType.description: Period type for the accounting periods of the financial year.

An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

get.description:
Retrieve financial periods for this tenant.

 The list of periods returned is dynamic, derived from the tenant's financial years. If a tenant does not have a particular financial year set, financial periods that would fall within that year are not returned in the list.

**Example:**

A tenant has a financial year set for the current year but not the previous year.
* The current period is not the first month of the year, but is within Quarter 1.
* The periods returned are: `ThisMonth`, `LastMonth`, `ThisQuarter`, `ThisYear` and `ThisYearToDate`.
* `LastQuarter` and `LastYear` are not returned, because there is no previous year.

post.summary: v1 - Convert bank receipt to payment
post.description: Converts a bank receipt transaction into a named-entity payment. The bank receipt must be unallocated and fully completed before conversion. Creates a new payment transaction of the specified `TargetTransactionTypeId` with the bank receipt amount, entity, inherited valid dimensions, and optional inline allocations. The original bank receipt transaction is deleted after the payment is created.

parameters.name: X-Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value, such as a GUID, generated by the client. An idempotency key enables the server to recognize subsequent retries of the same request and so avoid repeating the same operation. A request is processed only once per idempotency key, which remains valid for seven days.

TargetTransactionTypeId.description: The human-readable code of the target payment transaction type, for example, `CustomerReceipt`. Must not be `BankReceipt`. Must reference an active payment transaction type that always requires an identified entity — anonymous or suspense payments are not permitted as a conversion target.

Date.description: The transaction date for the new payment record created from this conversion.

Entity.description: The customer entity to associate with the new payment. Always required — conversion always produces a non-suspense payment with an identified entity.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the customer entity.

Allocations.description: Optional inline allocations to apply to the newly created payment. Each entry allocates the payment against the specified trade document. For payment types that do not permit on-account balances, allocations are mandatory and must fully settle the converted amount.

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.sandbox.sbc.sage.com")

payload = "{\"Date\":\"2021-01-01T08:49:36.940Z\",\"Draft\":false,\"BankAccount\":{\"Id\":\"0ee85e7f-2f5e-949c-3a8e-39f55c37aa1a\"},\"Reference\":\"RK5POBZNT7IH\",\"AdditionalReference\":\"RK5POBZNT7IH\",\"External\":{\"Id\":\"1ANUCGPYU552\",\"Source\":\"Accounting\",\"Number\":\"1ANUCGPYU552\"},\"Amount\":100,\"TreatAs\":\"Credit\",\"Prediction\":{\"PredictionExists\":true,\"PredictionReviewed\":true},\"Review\":{\"Reviewed\":false,\"Flagged\":false},\"Dimensions\":[{\"Dimension\":{\"Id\":\"CostCentre\"},\"DimensionTags\":[{\"Id\":\"CostCentre01\"}]},{\"Dimension\":{\"Id\":\"CostCentre\"},\"DimensionTags\":[{\"Id\":\"CostCentre02\"}]}]}"

headers = {
    'Content-Type': "application/json",

    }

conn.request("PUT", "/transaction/v1/tenant/%7BTenantId%7D/journals/%7BJournalTypeId%7D/%7BJournalId%7D", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

schema.title: V1UpdateSalesInvoiceRequestModel
schema.description: Request model for V1 Update Sales Invoice.

Date.description: The date and time of the sales invoice, as provided by the user of the client application. Must conform to the 'date-time' format defined in [RFC3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.html#section-5.6).

Reference.description: The manual reference of the sales invoice.

AdditionalReference.description: The additional reference of the sales invoice.

Description.description: The description of the sales invoice.

DueDate.description: The due date of the sales invoice, as provided by the user of the client application. Must conform to the 'date-time' format defined in [RFC3339](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3339.html#section-5.6).

Id.description: The unique identifier of the legacy sales invoice in the external system that generated it.

Source.description: The external source system that generated the legacy sales invoice.

Number.description: The external document number of the legacy sales invoice in the external system that generated it.

Customer.description: The customer associated with the sales invoice.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the customer.

Name.description: The name of the customer.

PhoneNumber.description: The phone number of the customer.

EmailAddress.description: The email address of the customer.

Addresses.description: A list of delivery and billing addresses for the sales invoice.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the sales invoice address to update.

AddressType.description: The address type. Only `BillingAddress` and `DeliveryAddress` are supported.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the address type.

AddressLine1.description: The first line of the address.

AddressLine2.description: The second line of the address.

PostCode.description: The postal/ZIP code of the address.

CountryCode.description: The ISO country code of the address.

Locale.description: The locale details for the address.

Id.description: The identifier of the address locale.

Currency.description: The currency details of the sales invoice.

Code.description: The ISO code of the currency.

ExchangeRate.description: The exchange rate used to calculate base-currency amounts.

PaymentBankAccountId.description: The unique identifier of the preferred bank account used for payment.

BankDetails.description: The bank details on the sales invoice.

PaymentDetails.description: The payment details on the sales invoice.

TermsAndConditions.description: The terms and conditions of the sales invoice.

FootNote.description: The footnote on the sales invoice.

AmountMethod.description: Whether the amount on the sales invoice item is calculated based on units and price or on a total amount.

EnableElectronicPayment.description: If `true` and the transaction type supports payment requests, then a payment request is generated in the Payment Acceptance Service.

Withholding.description: Withholding type details of the sales invoice.

WithholdingTypeId.description: The unique identifier of the withholding type applicable to this sales invoice. Used to determine the withholding tax rate, for example, CIS withholding rates of 0%, 20%, or 30%.

Sent.description: If `true`, the sales invoice is marked as sent by external means and no email tracking will be attempted. If omitted or `false`, the existing email delivery status is preserved unless the update posts a draft invoice.

Items.description: The items of the sales invoice.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the sales invoice item.

Order.description: The order of the line item within the sales invoice. If `null`, defaults to 0.

Product.description: The product details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the product.

ProductCategory.description: The product category details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the product category.

Description.description: The description of the sales invoice item.

Units.description: The number of units of the sales invoice item.

UnitPrice.description: The unit price of the sales invoice item.

Amount.description: The amount of the sales invoice item.

AmountType.description: Specifies whether taxes are included in the unit prices of the sales invoice. The value depends on how the journal type is configured in the service template.

Tax.description: Tax details of the sales invoice item.

TaxGroup.description: Tax group details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The identifier of the tax group, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

TaxTreatment.description: Tax treatment details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The identifier of the tax treatment, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

TaxItemType.description: Tax item type details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The identifier of the tax item type, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

TaxCode.description: Tax code details of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The identifier of the tax code, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

TaxAmount.description: The tax amount of the sales invoice item, as provided by the client application.

Withholding.description: Withholding type details of the sales invoice item.

IsWithholdingItem.description: Indicates whether this item is subject to withholding tax. When `true`, the withheld amount is calculated using the withholding rate from the sales invoice's `WithholdingTypeId`.

Dimensions.description: The dimensions of the sales invoice item.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the dimension, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

DimensionTags.description: The dimension tags of the specified dimension.

Id.description: The identifier of the dimension tag, expressed as a UUID or a human-readable code.

Each item in the request applies a portion of the payment's unallocated balance against the outstanding balance of the specified trade document. The transaction type pair (source and target) must be configured as a valid allocation relationship. Outstanding balances and payment statuses are updated accordingly.

Each item links a source payment to a target trade document for the specified amount. `SourceTransactionId` is the ID of the payment, such as a customer receipt, and `TargetTransactionId` is the ID of the trade document, such as a sales invoice. requestmodel.title: V1PostTabularReportExecuteRequestModel
requestmodel.description: Request body for executing a tabular report. In Phase 1, Grouping must be empty or omitted. LayoutKey, Filters, Sorting, Paging, Search, and Columns are all supported in Phase 1.

LayoutKey.description: The key of the designer layout to apply. Defaults to the report's `IsDefault=true` layout if omitted. Template-defined layouts are immutable.

UserLayoutId.description: The ID of the saved personal user layout to apply. Takes precedence over `LayoutKey` when set. Ownership scope: the layout must belong to the current tenant and user. Required when a personal layout is supplied.

Filters.description: Filter values to apply to the execution. Each entry must match a `FilterKey` value in the tabular filter definitions template for the report.

FilterKey.description: Identifies which filter this entry applies to.

Value.description: Filter value. The value shape is determined by the configured filter: use a scalar for single-value filters or an array for multi-value filters used with `In` or `NotIn`.

Sorting.description: Sort specification, applied in `Priority` order. Only sortable fields are accepted.

Field.description: Logical field key to sort by.

Priority.description: Sort priority when multiple sort fields are specified. Lower number is applied first.

Grouping.description: Reserved for a future grouping capability. In Phase 1, omit this property or send an empty array; a non-empty array returns 400 GroupingNotSupported.

Field.description: Logical field key to group by. Must have `CanGroup=true` in the tabular fields template.

Expanded.description: When `true` the group is expanded and data rows are included. When `false` only the group header and footer are returned.

Paging.description: Pagination parameters for the first result page. To navigate subsequent pages, use *Get tabular report execution* `page` and `page-items` query parameters with the execution endpoint without re-sending the execute body.

PageSize.description: Number of rows per page. Values above the configured tabular maximum are capped at runtime.

Search.description: Free-text search applied across `IsSearchable=true` columns. Only active when tabular support searching is true. Omit to disable search.

Columns.description: Explicit list of field keys to include in the response. Overrides the active layout's visibility settings. Capped to the tabular maximum projected columns value. Omit to use the layout defaults.

Id.description: The unique ID of the created record.

Color.description: Color that can be applied to cells. Consuming applications can associate each enum value with a color, which is applied when the enum is specified.

Type.description: Data type of the cells. `MultilineString` allows the `Header.Formatting.Columns.MultilineValue` object to be populated with an array of strings for display in the report header.

TabularHeaderCell.title: TabularHeaderCell
TabularHeaderCell.description: A display column in a tabular execution header.

Value.description: The display value for the column.

Width.description: The resolved display width from the active tabular layout or column definition.

Value.description: Display value for the cell.

TabularExecutionRow.title: TabularExecutionRow
TabularExecutionRow.description: A row in the tabular execution payload.

Type.description: Data contains report values. `GroupHeader` introduces a group and `GroupFooter` contains its subtotal values when grouping is enabled.

Field.description: Grouping field key for GroupHeader and GroupFooter rows.

Value.description: Grouping field value for GroupHeader and GroupFooter rows.

Count.description: Row count in the group for GroupHeader rows.

Expanded.description: Whether a group is expanded for GroupHeader rows.

TabularAggregation.title: TabularAggregation
TabularAggregation.description: Aggregation result entry for a tabular execution.

TabularExecutionMetadata.title: TabularExecutionMetadata
TabularExecutionMetadata.description: Context for interpreting the tabular execution result.

GroupingMode.description: Where grouping was applied. Phase 1 executions return `None`.

FetchedRowsForGrouping.description: Number of datasource rows fetched to perform engine-side grouping. Returns `0` when grouping is not engine-side.

ReportNote.description: Configured report note for the executed report.

responsemodel-2.title: V1GetTabularReportExecutionResponseModel
responsemodel-2.description: Completed result for a tabular execution. Obtain the execution ID from Execute, then poll this resource until it returns 200.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the execution.

Name.description: The report name.

Description.description: The report description.

LastRunDate.description: The execution completion timestamp in ISO 8601 UTC format.

Header.description: Display columns in the order used by each data row.

Rows.description: Ordered result rows. Data rows contain report values; GroupHeader and GroupFooter rows describe groups when grouping is enabled.

Aggregations.description: Computed totals keyed by field. Each value identifies its calculation type and scope.

example.Name: Open Invoices

requestmodel-2.title: V1PostTabularReportExportRequestModel
requestmodel-2.description: Request body for exporting a tabular report. Similar to execute request but includes Format field and fetches all pages from the datasource regardless of Paging settings — Paging in this body is ignored.

LayoutKey.description: The key of the designer layout to apply. Defaults to the report's `IsDefault=true` layout if omitted. Template-defined layouts are immutable.

UserLayoutId.description: The ID of the saved personal user layout to apply. Takes precedence over `LayoutKey` when set. Ownership scope: the layout must belong to the current tenant and user. Required when a personal layout is supplied.

Filters.description: Filter values to apply to this export. Each entry must match a filter key in the tabular filter definitions template for this report.

FilterKey.description: Identifies which filter this entry applies to.

Value.description: Filter value. May be a scalar or an array when the filter allows multiple values and `Operator` is `In` or `NotIn`.

Sorting.description: Sort specification, in `Priority` order. Only `IsSortable=true` fields are accepted.

Field.description: Logical field key to sort by.

Priority.description: Sort priority when multiple sort fields are specified. Lower number is applied first.

Grouping.description: In Phase 1, a non-empty array returns `400 Grouping not supported`. In Phase 2, specifies the grouping fields; only `CanGroup=true` fields are accepted.

Field.description: Logical field key to group by. Must have `CanGroup=true` in the tabular fields template.

Expanded.description: When `true` the group is expanded and data rows are included. When `false` only the group header and footer are returned.

Page.description: The page number. Ignored for exports.

PageSize.description: Number of rows per page. Ignored for exports; values are normalized by the runtime before export processing.

Search.description: Free-text search applied across `IsSearchable=true` columns. Only active when `Tabular.Supports.Searching` is true. Omit to disable search.

Columns.description: Explicit list of field keys to include in the export. Overrides the active layout's visibility settings. Capped to the tabular maximum projected columns value. Omit to use the layout defaults.

Format.description: The export file format. Supported values are EXCEL, CSV, and PDF. Values are case-insensitive.

responsemodel-3.title: V1GetTabularReportConfigurationResponseModel
responsemodel-3.description: Response model for GET /tabular/{ReportType}/{ReportSubType}/configuration. Returns the effective report definition including datasource capabilities, full column catalog with active layout visibility overlay, filter definitions, one unified collection of designer, tenant, and caller-owned user layouts, and export settings. Layout metadata is returned by default; `LayoutJson` is included when the `LayoutJson` expansion is requested. Template-defined layouts are immutable.

Id.description: The unique identifier of the report.

Name.description: Display name.

Description.description: Short description.

Version.description: Schema version, for layout migration tracking.

Capabilities.description: Effective capability flags after resolving datasource capabilities, report options' *Tabular.Supports.** *and* tenant overrides. All three layers must agree for a capability to be enabled.

Grouping.description: Phase 2 only — always false in Phase 1.

Aggregations.description: Phase 2 only — always false in Phase 1.

Columns.description: Full column catalog. All columns are returned; `IsVisible` reflects the active layout. Columns with `IsVisible=false` and `CanHide=true` can be toggled by the user via a personal layout.

Field.description: Logical field key.

IsVisible.description: Effective visibility from the active layout.

IsRequired.description: When `true`, always present in the response regardless of visibility setting.

CanGroup.description: Whether this field can be used as a grouping dimension (Phase 2 only).

CanTotal.description: Whether this field can be aggregated.

AllowUserChange.description: When `false`, users cannot change the value.

DefaultValue.description: Default filter value. Null if no default. May be a string, number, boolean, or array depending on the filter's `DataType`.

ParameterBinding.description: How the filter maps to a datasource parameter.

Layouts.description: All active selectable layouts visible to the caller: designer layouts, tenant layouts, and layouts owned by the authenticated caller. The normal response contains metadata only; `LayoutJson` is included for every item when the `LayoutJson` expansion is requested.

Scope.description: The ownership scope of the layout. User layouts belong only to the authenticated caller.

BaseLayoutKey.description: The designer layout key from which a tenant or user layout was derived.

LayoutJson.description: The layout definition. Omitted unless the LayoutJson expansion is requested.

Financial period settings for the current tenant. The list of periods returned is dynamic, derived from the tenant's financial years.

If a tenant does not have a particular financial year set, financial periods that would fall within that year are not returned in the list.

*Example:*
* A tenant has a financial year set for the current year but not the previous year.
* The current period is not the first month of the year, but is within Quarter 1.
* The periods returned are: `ThisMonth`, `LastMonth`, `ThisQuarter`, `ThisYear` and `ThisYearToDate`.
* `LastQuarter` and `LastYear` are not returned, because there is no previous year.
